$comment: Q78.1: the elevation ladder, the separation cues and the z-index procedure, as data. The library’s Elevation and layering page and the agent guide read this file, and docs/materials.md (Elevation: one ladder) matches it; edit it here, never in a page.

ladder.name: Sunken
ladder.examples: Navigation rail, code block, board column, empty track
ladder.use: A region set into the page that holds other things.
ladder.never: A shadow or an outline: a well is lower, not a box.
ladder.detail: One tone step down; no shadow, no outline.

ladder.name: Canvas
ladder.examples: The page, a layout’s main region
ladder.use: The page itself. Most content needs nothing above it.
ladder.never: Panels around whole regions: enclosure noise.
ladder.detail: color.bg; no panels around whole regions.

ladder.name: Raised
ladder.material: MT3 raised, MT4 tint, MT5 control fill
ladder.examples: Card, panel, field, the current item
ladder.use: Something set onto the page that a person reads or works in.
ladder.never: A shadow at rest: content doesn’t float.
ladder.detail: One tone step up; a hairline only where tone can’t separate; never a shadow at rest.

ladder.name: Chrome
ladder.examples: Sticky site header, title bar, docked toolbar
ladder.use: A bar that stays put while the page scrolls under it.
ladder.never: A shadow at rest, or floating material for a docked bar.
ladder.detail: layer.sticky; frosted when the global setting is on; hairline only while content is under it; no shadow at rest.

ladder.name: Floating
ladder.examples: Menu, select list, popover, date picker, tooltip, floating toolbar, notification
ladder.use: Something that opens over the page without blocking it.
ladder.never: Glass on glass: a floating surface inside another is solid.
ladder.detail: Top layer; shadow.raised when anchored to a trigger, shadow.overlay when free; frosted when on; never glass on glass.

ladder.name: Modal
ladder.use: Something that blocks the page until it’s answered, over a dimmed page.
ladder.never: Frosted: the scrim already separates and the content is text.
ladder.detail: layer.overlay scrim + layer.dialog surface; shadow.overlay; always solid.

cues.name: Tone
cues.says: A different surface at the same height
cues.use: First choice: a card or panel on the page. In dark mode nearer is lighter.

cues.name: Hairline
cues.says: An edge tone alone can’t show
cues.use: Where tone is too close, or in more contrast. Always a full outline, never one side.

cues.name: Shadow, anchored
cues.says: It floats just above, tied to what opened it

cues.name: Shadow, free
cues.says: It floats well above, on its own
cues.use: A floating toolbar, a notification, a dialog over its scrim.

cues.name: Tint
cues.says: This one, among many: a state, not a height
cues.use: The current page, a selected row, a person’s own chat bubble.

zIndex: Does it need to be above anything at all? Content stays at layer.base in source order; nothing raises itself to win.
Does it stay while content scrolls under it? It’s chrome: layer.sticky, inside its own scroll region.

Does it open from a trigger or float free? Open it in the browser’s top layer (the popover attribute, or a modal dialog element); its layer token (layer.popover, layer.toast, layer.tooltip) is only the fallback order.
Does it block the page? A modal dialog element, with layer.overlay for the scrim and layer.dialog for the surface.
Does a component order its own parts? layer.behind and layer.raised, with isolation: isolate on the element that holds them, so the order never leaks.

Still hidden behind something? Find the ancestor that starts a stacking context (a transform, filter, opacity below 1, isolation or a z-index) and move the thing to the top layer or to the layout’s overlay. Never a bigger number.

Write z-index only as var(--layer-*) or a component token that aliases one (c.<part>.layer). npm run check:layers fails on a number, an inline zIndex, a component stacking token that aliases no layer, and inside layers without isolation, in core, the library, templates and the example app.
